headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Adding Built-In Storage to Your Bathroom Remodel
articleBody:
Adding extra storage during a bathroom renovation seems straightforward until you find yourself squeezing past half-opened doors or staring at warped shelving. Because bathrooms combine daily humidity with compact square footage, minor planning errors lead to frustrating functional headaches.

### Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Covering emergency shutoff valves or cleanout panels: Building cabinetry over shutoffs makes resolving future plumbing leaks slow and destructive. Always leave valves accessible.
- Relying on basic drywall anchors for heavy hanging units: Storing full bottles of shampoo and heavy stacks of towels requires mounting cabinetry into structural wall studs or installed horizontal blocking.
- Using unsealed, standard-grade wood products: Standard particle board absorbs humidity rapidly, swelling around joints and peeling veneer within months. Choose moisture-resistant, factory-sealed materials.
- Forgetting drawer clearance around plumbing trap assemblies: Buying pre-made vanity drawers without checking where your P-trap and supply lines sit often requires field-modifying drawers and ruining storage space.
- Positioning open shelves directly in the shower splash zone: Open cubbies placed too close to shower enclosures catch overspray, creating constant water-spotting and mildew on stored linens.
- Overcrowding required fixture clearances: Placing bulky wall cabinets too close to the toilet or vanity edge violates standard comfort clearances and makes the room feel cramped.
